chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: concerning

Regarding a man who dies while women are with him and no man is with them, he said: “They should pour water from behind the cloth, wrap him in his shrouds from beneath the covering, perform salat in a row, and place him in his grave.” And regarding a woman who dies while men are with her and no woman is with them, he said: “They should pour water from behind the cloth, wrap her in her shrouds, perform salat, and bury her.”

Because the proper approach concerning these two reports is that we interpret them as indicating a kind of recommendation rather than obligation. We only prohibited women from washing men when they directly handle their bodies; but if water is poured over them, then there is no harm in that. As for the woman, it is also permissible for men to wash of her that which it was permissible for them to look at during her lifetime, namely the face and the hands, and more than that is not permissible. This is indicated by what al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar narrated, which we have already presented.

key_terms.أَكْفَانِهَا: the shrouds in which the deceased woman is wrapped
key_terms.أَكْفَانِهِ: the shrouds in which the deceased man is wrapped
key_terms.ٱلثَّوْبِ: the cloth behind which the water is poured
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءَ: water used for indirect washing of the deceased
key_terms.ٱلْوَجْهِ وَٱلْيَدَيْنِ: the parts of a woman that may be looked at and thus washed in this context

ai.seo_question: How should a deceased man or woman be washed and buried if only members of the opposite sex are present?
ai.summary: This report discusses the rulings for preparing the deceased when only members of the opposite sex are present. It states that washing may be done indirectly by pouring water from behind a cloth, with shrouding, funeral salat, and burial proceeding accordingly. The closing legal note explains that this is understood as a recommended allowance in such circumstances, while direct bodily contact remains restricted.
